dedupe_keys.name: production and carbon footprint of microbial oil from waste lemon peel extract supplementary material

description: Vittorio Senatore and Paola Branduardi publish supplementary and underlying data for microbial oil production from waste lemon peel extract. The source describes fermentation in two-litre bioreactors, lipid extraction and a carbon-footprint assessment of laboratory production. It also reports a simulation of the process in a 300-litre fermenter to examine how scale affects electricity consumption and environmental impact. The data therefore have a concrete role in modelling a chemical production process and examining process optimisation. Version 3 lists two underlying-data XLSX workbooks and two supplementary PDFs, including revised and earlier files. Their internal tables and differences were not inspected. A Zenodo deposit describes the same study and its earlier underlying workbook and supplementary PDF; their filenames and stated sizes match the earlier Mendeley descriptors, without a byte comparison. The repository provides metadata and access links, and the resource is free under CC BY 4.0. The geographic extent, study dates, spatial resolution and temporal sampling interval remain unknown. Laboratory measurements and the simulated scale-up must be kept distinct; the source does not establish industrial-scale performance. No files or paper bodies were retrieved. No related active catalogue resource was established.
